transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, my friends and an urgent care doctor keep insisting that I’m way too thin and need professional help. Personally, I don't really see what the big problem is with my weight being this low, but I'm here because they're making such a big deal out of it.
Are you afraid of gaining weight or becoming fat, or do you feel your body is larger than it really is? If not, what do you think is causing your low weight?

Yeah, to be honest, the thought of gaining weight really panics me; if I even think about eating something heavy like a burger, I worry I'll wake up looking softer the next day. When I look in the mirror, I don't see what others see—I just zero in on my stomach or thighs not looking razor-thin and feel like I've failed to stay disciplined.

Can you tell me how you’ve been keeping your weight this low—for example, by eating very little, exercising a lot, or doing things like vomiting, using laxatives, or diet pills? About how often does that happen?

Most days I keep my weight down strictly by barely eating, usually just powering through on black coffee and maybe a granola bar at night because I'm too busy painting or too broke for real meals. I don't use laxatives, diet pills, or throw up at all; it's really just about restricting what I eat.
Do you ever have episodes where you eat a much larger amount of food than most people would in a short time and feel unable to stop? If yes, how often does that happen?
No, I never have episodes like that where I lose control and overeat. My issue is the exact opposite, where I'm just focused on restricting my food and skipping meals altogether.
Have your menstrual periods changed or stopped since your weight dropped? If yes, when was your last period?
Actually, I'm a man, so I don't get menstrual periods. I'm a bit confused as to why you're asking me that, to be honest.
About how much do you weigh and how tall are you right now, and do you believe that weight is healthy for you?

I don't know my exact weight right now, only that my clothes are hanging off me and my belt is on the last loop. To be honest, I don't see my weight as a problem at all; to me, it's just a sign of my discipline and efficiency. I really think the urgent care doctor and my friends are just overreacting.

Have you had any physical problems from being this underweight, like dizziness or fainting, feeling very weak, your heart racing or beating slowly, or being unusually cold? If so, which of these has been happening?

I haven't noticed any heart issues or feeling unusually cold, but I do get incredibly weak and shaky, especially when I'm up on the ladder painting. It actually caused a minor fall recently, and I get so exhausted halfway through the day that I've had to cut my mural jobs short. Because of that lack of energy, I've also been skipping out on hikes and hanging out with friends.
Do you know your current weight or your lowest recent weight, and about how much weight have you lost over what period of time? If you don’t know the exact numbers, even an estimate is helpful.
I honestly don't know my exact weight or how much I've lost because I don't really weigh myself regularly. I just know that my clothes are hanging off me now and my belt is on its very last hole.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports anorexia nervosa, restricting type: the patient is markedly underweight by history, persistently restricts intake, has intense fear of weight gain, significant body-image distortion/overvaluation of thinness, and lacks recognition of the seriousness of the low weight. He denies binge eating and purging, supporting the restricting subtype pattern within F50.0. Functional and physical consequences from starvation are present.
